**One mistake I see repeatedly in critical infrastructure security compliance...**

In my experience, one of the most common errors I see in organizations seeking to comply with Canada's Bill C-8 is misclassifying their incident reporting requirements. Specifically, many companies assume that the 72-hour reporting rule applies only to security incidents, whereas it actually applies to **all** types of critical infrastructure security incidents, including non-security-related events like IT outages or environmental breaches.

**Consequences of this mistake:**

• Inaccurate reporting: Failing to report all incidents within the 72-hour window can lead to inaccurate reporting and a lack of transparency, which can damage trust with regulatory bodies and the public.
• Inadequate risk management: Misclassifying incident types can lead to inadequate risk management and mitigation strategies, putting the organization and its stakeholders at greater risk.
• Regulatory non-compliance: Non-compliance with the 72-hour reporting rule can result in significant fines and reputational damage.

**Solution:** To avoid this mistake, organizations should take a comprehensive approach to incident classification, involving both security and non-security incident types. This will ensure accurate reporting, effective risk management, and compliance with regulatory requirements.

**Have you seen this mistake crop up in your own organization? How do you ensure accurate incident reporting under Bill C-8?**
